Bondservice
BOND-ser-vis
n. (compulsory labour exacted as tribute; the levy Solomon laid on the remnant of the Canaanites)
From bond, a fetter or obligation, and service. The Authorized Version uses it once, of the tribute Solomon levied on the peoples left in the land, distinguished in the next verse from what he did with Israelites.

Biblical Definition

Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day. The Chronicler-like care of the next verse matters: but of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen; but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen. Whatever Solomon did with the remnant of the nations, the covenant people were not made slaves — and yet the story does not end there. When Rehoboam came to Shechem, the complaint of the ten tribes was precisely about the burden: thy father made our yoke grievous; now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee. Rehoboam took the young men's counsel, promised to add to the yoke, and lost ten tribes in an afternoon. The New Testament takes the whole vocabulary of yokes and bondage and settles it in one verse: stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): slavery; the condition of a bond servant; in Scripture, the compulsory labour Solomon levied on the remnant of the Canaanite nations.

expand to see more

BONDSERVICE, n. The condition of a bond servant; slavery.

BONDMAN, n. A man slave, or one bound to service without wages.

TRIBUTE, n. An annual or stated sum of money paid by one prince or nation to another.

YOKE, n. Something that binds or connects; a mark of servitude; slavery; bondage.

LIBERTY, n. Freedom from restraint; in a religious sense, freedom from the bondage of sin and from the ceremonial law.

Key Scripture

1Ki 9:21 — "Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day."

1Ki 9:22 — "But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen."

1Ki 12:4 — "Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee."

Gal 5:1 — "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage."

Modern Corruption

Scripture's record of servitude is read either as divine endorsement of chattel slavery or as proof the Bible is worthless on the subject; the texts distinguish carefully between forms of service and press toward the liberty Christ purchased.

expand to see more

Two bad readings meet here. The first takes any biblical mention of servitude as approval of the race-based chattel slavery of the modern era — a system the Bible condemns at its root, since Exodus makes manstealing a capital crime and 1 Timothy lists menstealers with murderers and perjurers among those the law is made for. The second discards the Scriptures as compromised. Both skip the actual text, which regulates existing servitude with release years, sabbath rest for servants, protection from mutilation, and refuge for the runaway, and which draws a line here between the levy on the nations and the treatment of Israelites.

The New Testament's trajectory is unmistakable to anyone who reads Philemon. Paul sends a runaway back not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, and tells the master to receive him as myself. He tells servants to serve heartily as to the Lord and masters to give what is just and equal, knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven. And he tells the servant who can be made free to use it rather. The gospel does not bless the yoke; it undermines it, and it begins by naming the deepest bondage, which is sin, and the liberty Christ bought from it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mac 'obed (H4522, H5647), a levy of serving; 'ebed (H5650), a servant or bondman; 'ol (H5923), a yoke.

expand to see more

Hebrew mac (H4522) — a burden, a levy, forced labour; a tribute of bondservice.

Hebrew 'abad (H5647) — to work, to serve, to labour; the service levied.

Hebrew 'ebed (H5650) — a servant, a bondman; did Solomon make no bondmen of Israel.

Hebrew 'ol (H5923) — a yoke; thy father made our yoke grievous.

Greek eleutheria (G1657) — liberty, freedom; the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.

Usage

"“did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice” — the single occurrence."

"“of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen” — the distinction drawn."

"“be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage” — where the whole vocabulary lands."
